comment: Extremely nit-picky when grading. Took off 10% on my final project (which was working perfectly and was a week early) because 'I declared a variable and did not use it'. This was the only 'mistake' she found in the 4 java files, and decided that was worth 10% of my final project grade. She responded to my email saying I should have done better(???)

Dr. Jiang frequently tries to explain the concepts in different ways to make sure everyone is understanding them.  There were many group coding projects, some of them with extra credit opportunities. Feedback was usually good and the final was reasonable.

I did not learn much from her class and homework was very confusing. Your whole grade is heavily depends on your mid-term and your final project, nothing else. She is not helpful at all when I find her after class, I don't really get my questions answered in office hour. I would not recommend her if you actually want to learn something in a class.

The class lectures were basically straight from the textbook, so you could get away without reading if necessary. The homework is 40% of the grade and is challenging, but there's extra credit and you have a week per assignment so if you plan well you'll be fine. Answers questions at 1 AM. Exam was worth 25% and was hard but was what she taught us.

This class is super hard, so make sure you go to class. Prof. Jiang is new, so there may be some things that will make this class tedious for everyone. The class consists of around 12 hw projects, no midterm, and lecture heavy. Final exam is mostly from the lectures and the labs. READ the txtbook, try on the labs, ask questions and you will pass.

CMSC221 is a really difficult class, and Prof. Jiang recognizes that. She's new at UR, but is very receptive to feedback. Very nice and willing to help if you ask questions, but sometimes you have to ask a lot of questions in order to get what you need. Very quiet and sometimes hard to understand, but wants to help if you just reach out and ask.
